Flooding Halts Oil & Gas Operations Across Northern Italy

Heavy rainfall causing severe flooding across northern Italy has brought significant disruption to the oil and gas producers industry, with multiple sites and transport routes affected as the weather event continues. The Po River, which runs through the heart of Italy’s industrial corridor, has burst its banks in several areas since Tuesday, inundating access roads and forcing the temporary shutdown of key production facilities.

Several operators, including NordEnergia S.p.A. and Valpadana Resources, have suspended extraction and refining activities at their sites in Emilia-Romagna and Lombardy. “Our main refinery near Piacenza has been inaccessible since early Wednesday due to floodwater covering the main approach roads,” said Giulia Romani, spokesperson for NordEnergia. “We are prioritising worker safety and cooperating with emergency services.”

The Italian Oil Producers Association (AIP) estimates that approximately 35% of the region’s production capacity is currently offline. “Initial indications suggest daily output losses in the range of 18,000 to 22,000 barrels of oil equivalent,” said Luca Ferrara, AIP’s head of industry analysis. “Restoration will depend on how quickly water levels recede and the extent of site damage, which is still unknown.”

Pipeline infrastructure has also been affected, with flooding disrupting scheduled deliveries to regional storage hubs. Several gas processing plants have reported precautionary shutdowns due to high water levels. Trade union representatives have voiced concerns over the impact on local employment if operations remain suspended for an extended period.

Meteorologists forecast continued heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours, raising the risk of further flooding along key transport corridors. Industry officials are monitoring the situation and preparing for a prolonged operational standstill as the natural event unfolds.
